links.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of patient materials before and after ChatGPT modification
links.effect: ChatGPT improved FRE of the 10 least readable articles (19.7 ± 4.4 vs. 56.9 ± 5.9, p < 0.001), from university to 10th grade level, still above the recommended sixth-grade level.
links.quote: ChatGPT improved FRE readability of the 10 least readable online articles (19.7 ± 4.4 vs. 56.9 ± 5.9, p < 0.001), from university to 10th grade level.

links.outcome: Reading level of online and AI-generated patient education materials versus recommended literacy
links.effect: Existing ESBS articles were unreadable (mean FRE 39.4 ± 12.4); ChatGPT-modified articles reached about 10th grade level, and the generated article had FRE 38.9, above the recommended sixth-grade level.
links.quote: ChatGPT improves the readability of articles, though most still remain above the recommended literacy level for patient education materials.

unlisted_practices: Using ChatGPT with iterative queries to generate patient education materials de novo
Assessing reliability and quality of patient education materials with the DISCERN instrument

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates ChatGPT for simplifying and generating patient education materials for endoscopic skull base surgery using readability formulas and DISCERN quality scoring, without testing a specific operational deployment safeguard.
